import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 60

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/60](https://www.erdosproblems.com/60)
- [HeMaYa21] He, J. and Ma, J. and Yang, T., *Some extremal results on 4-cycles*. Journal of
  Combinatorial Theory B (2021).
-/

namespace Erdos60

open SimpleGraph Filter
open scoped Real

/--
Does every graph on $n$ vertices with $>\mathrm{ex}(n;C_4)$ edges contain $\gg n^{1/2}$ many
copies of $C_4$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_60 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
          (c * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/- ## Variants and partial results -/

/--
He, Ma, and Yang [HeMaYa21] proved the conjecture when $n = q^2 + q + 1$ for some even integer $q$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧
      ∀ (q : ℕ) (_hq : Even q),
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (q^2 + q + 1))) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          (extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
          (c * Real.sqrt ((q^2 + q + 1) : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Simonovits conjectured that at least 2 copies of $C_4$ are guaranteed.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_60.variants.two_copies :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        (extremalNumber n (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
        (2 ≤ { H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard) := by
  sorry

end Erdos60

findings.description: The named partial result is overstated: the theorem quantifies over every even q and assumes only extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card. He–Ma–Yang's result for general even q instead uses the explicit edge threshold M = q(q+1)^2/2. Their corollary at one edge above the actual extremal number is stated for q = 2^k. These thresholds genuinely differ: the same paper proves ex(q^2+q+1,C4) ≤ M − 0.2q for infinitely many even q having no projective plane. For large such q, adding an edge to an extremal C4-free graph gives a graph satisfying the Lean hypothesis with at most M edges, outside the published theorem's scope. The website's summary repeats the overbroad even-q formulation, but the cited primary paper distinguishes the two claims explicitly.
findings.source_evidence: He, Ma and Yang, Some extremal results on 4-cycles, §1, Theorem 1.3: for even q ≥ 10^12, G has q^2+q+1 vertices and q(q+1)^2/2+1 edges. The following paragraph deduces the ex(n,C4)+1 result specifically 'For q = 2^k where k ≥ 40'. The paragraph following Theorem 1.2 gives the strict extremal-number improvement for infinitely many even q without projective planes. Author's text: http://staff.ustc.edu.cn/~jiema/c4-turan.pdf. These distinctions are also stated in §1 of arXiv:1912.00986v4.
findings.suggested_fix: If retaining the extremalNumber hypothesis, restrict q to even prime powers—for example, add an assumption IsPrimePow q alongside Even q, equivalently use q = 2^k with k > 0—and correct the docstring accordingly. The existential positive constant allows the finitely many small q to be retained. Alternatively, state the general-even-q result using q * (q + 1)^2 / 2 < G.edgeFinset.card for sufficiently large even q.

status_issues.source_status: The cited account still presents the general-n two-copy assertion as the weak Erdős–Simonovits conjecture, rather than an established result. The He–Ma–Yang results concern special vertex counts and do not provide this all-sufficiently-large-n conclusion.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/60 remains marked OPEN and says Erdős and Simonovits 'could not even prove that at least 2 copies of C4 are guaranteed'. More explicitly, arXiv:1912.00986v4, §1, describes 'A weak version ... [which] asserted that h(n) ≥ 2 for large n', while stating the proved ex(n,C4)+1 corollary only for q=2^k. No general-n solution is recorded in the cited sources.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change two_copies to category research open unless an additional accepted general-n proof can be supplied. Keep its mathematical statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The source's number of C4 copies and asymptotic lower-bound notation are represented by Set.ncard of isomorphic subgraphs and an eventual quantifier on ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A subgraph whose coe is isomorphic to cycleGraph 4 is exactly an ordinary, unlabelled C4 copy. It need not be induced, and different cycle edge sets on the same four vertices remain distinct. G.Subgraph is finite for G on Fin n, so ncard never takes its infinite-set default. In /workspace/review/finite_extension.lean I proved that this ncard equals G.copyCount (cycleGraph 4), and proved the full statement equivalent to one with an explicit threshold N and the bound for every n ≥ N.

reformulations.difference: The primary literature formulates the weak conjecture as h(n) ≥ 2, where h(n) minimizes the copy count among graphs with exactly ex(n,C4)+1 edges; Lean quantifies over every graph with more than ex(n,C4) edges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any graph above the extremal threshold has a spanning subgraph with exactly ex(n,C4)+1 edges, obtained by deleting surplus edges. Every C4 in that subgraph remains a C4 in the original graph. Thus the bound at exactly one excess edge implies the bound for every larger edge count, and the converse follows by specialization. The source explicitly requires sufficiently large n, matching the eventual quantifier.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. Scratch proofs establish that the edge hypothesis is impossible for n<4 and is attainable by the complete graph for every n≥4. They also establish positivity of the copy count whenever the extremal threshold is exceeded. Importantly, the universal-q quantifier is not a separate defect: for any fixed restriction on q, I proved the eventual and all-q positive-constant formulations equivalent, using sqrt(q²+q+1)≤q+1 and shrinking the constant on the finite initial segment. Finite enumeration gave (n, ex(n,C4), minimum copies at ex+1) = (4,4,1), (5,6,2), (6,7,1), consistent with the need for an eventual two-copy statement. Experiments are in /workspace/review/; the successful proof checks do not depend on the problem's sorry theorems. The reviewed file still matches its committed hash.

submission.summary: Added IsPrimePow q alongside Even q, restricting the partial result to even prime powers, and updated its docstring accordingly. Other declarations were left unchanged. The required compile command succeeded with only the existing 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
